output_json.patch_notes: Added a private static helper `resolveDestination(File outputDir, String name)` in ZipUtil that builds `new File(outputDir, name)`, compares its canonical path against the canonical path of outputDir, and throws the project's `org.zeroturnaround.zip.ZipException` (a RuntimeException) when the destination is not equal to or beneath outputDir (using `canonicalDir + File.separator` as the containment prefix to avoid sibling-prefix false negatives). IOException during canonicalization is rethrown via the existing ZipExceptionUtil.rethrow. Replaced the four raw `new File(outputDir/parentDirectory, name)` joins in Unpacker.process (line ~1152), BackslashUnpacker.process (both the per-segment directory creation and the destination file, lines ~1214/1220/1225), and Unwraper.process (line ~1260) with calls to the helper. In BackslashUnpacker each split segment is validated against its immediate parent, which blocks `..` segments as well. Added ZipSlipTest with a traversal-rejection test (entry `../escaped.txt` must throw and must not create the escaped file) and a positive test (a normal `sub/legit.txt` entry still extracts).
output_json.risk_notes: The fix relies on File.getCanonicalPath(), which resolves symlinks; extraction into a directory that is itself reached through a symlink is still permitted as long as the final canonical destination stays within the canonical output directory, so legitimate use is preserved. Behavior change: malicious/malformed archives now throw ZipException (a RuntimeException) instead of silently writing traversal files — callers that previously relied on such writes would break, but that is the intended security hardening. Full `mvn -B test` shows one pre-existing unrelated failure, testPreserveWriteFlag(FilePermissionsTest), which also fails on the unpatched baseline (tests run as root in the container, so the write-flag assertion cannot hold); all other 117 tests pass including the two new ones.
output_json.summary: Fixed a Zip Slip (CWE-022 path traversal) vulnerability in org.zeroturnaround.zip.ZipUtil. All three extraction branches (Unpacker, BackslashUnpacker, Unwraper) joined an attacker-controlled ZIP entry name to the output directory via `new File(outputDir, name)` with no validation, allowing entries like `../escaped.txt` to write outside the intended directory. Added a `resolveDestination(File outputDir, String name)` helper that canonicalizes the resolved destination and throws a ZipException if it escapes the output directory, then routed all three sinks through it. The validated POV now reports SAFE (exit 1) after previously reporting VULNERABLE (exit 0).
